incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images of Leal to promote fraudulent immigration services, including offering US residency for $2,200 cash payments. The scams typically direct victims to contact phone numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payment through digital payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

Leal first discovered the scheme in October when potential clients began calling his office, but the situation has dramatically worsened in recent months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud. He advises immigrants to verify identities of legal service providers online and avoid anyone requesting immediate payments through digital apps.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article claiming Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock had a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler never actually occurred. The fabricated piece promoted Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform that Australian authorities warn against. This type of scam is becoming increasingly common as artificial intelligence makes deceptive content easier to create and more convincing to potential victims.

Australian Securities and Investments Commission research reveals that investment scams using deepfake images and videos of celebrities and politicians are rising sharply. Last year, the regulator removed 19,400 scams total, including 7,051 fake investment platforms and 5,476 phishing scams. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Alan Kohler, and billionaire Gina Rinehart are among the most commonly impersonated Australians. ASIC urges consumers to verify financial services licenses through official registers and warns that polished content and familiar branding do not guarantee legitimacy.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Oura, the smart ring company valued at approximately eleven billion dollars, accusing it of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The lawsuit, filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco on Thursday, alleges that Oura's rings cost three hundred dollars or more and are marketed as capable of detecting sleep stages with ninety-five percent accuracy comparable to hospital sleep labs. However, the suit claims the devices cannot actually measure the physiological signals needed for accurate sleep stage detection and instead rely on unreliable artificial intelligence predictions.

Oura disputed the allegations through a company spokesperson, stating that the rings use multiple physiological signals including heart rate, movement, and temperature to estimate sleep stages. The company notes that its sleep staging has been validated through peer-reviewed scientific studies and compared favorably against polysomnography, the clinical standard. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation affected customers might receive if successful. This marks the second lawsuit against Oura, following a previous class action alleging the company collected personal information without consent for two years.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi virtual environments since April 2026. The group has developed a Linux ransomware variant that encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi-specific mode to shut down running virtual machines before encryption. Attackers used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan victim networks for ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers. Aurora operates a data leak site and targets organizations across multiple countries.

In a notable development, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The AI agent performed reconnaissance tasks, attempted privilege escalation attacks, and executed network scanning tools, though many initial attempts failed and required multiple refinements. Gambit also identified a second Aurora cluster responsible for attacks across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina, using different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Chaac Pizza Northeast, a major Pizza Hut franchisee operating approximately 111 restaurants across the Northeast, filed a lawsuit in Texas Business Court in May alleging that Pizza Hut's mandatory implementation of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management system, caused severe operational problems and approximately $100 million in damages. The system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen workflows, causing drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering completed pizzas immediately, resulting in longer delivery times and reduced customer satisfaction. Prior to the rollout in 2024, Chaac's deliveries arrived within thirty minutes over ninety percent of the time with double-digit sales growth, but afterward, New York City sales dropped from positive 10.19% growth to negative 9.78% year-over-year.

The franchisee claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training on the system and ignored requests for support while mandating its continued use. Chaac argues Pizza Hut breached their franchise agreement by implementing software without exercising reasonable business judgment or accommodating the franchisee's delivery model. The lawsuit seeks over $100 million in damages plus attorney fees. Pizza Hut declined detailed comment, stating it would respond through legal channels, while the broader Pizza Hut brand continues facing business challenges, with parent company Yum! Brands planning to close 250 US locations.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers have been sending personalized emails impersonating Terry Gross, host of the NPR program Fresh Air, to solicit fees from potential interview guests. Authors, entertainers and other public figures have received highly detailed messages that reference their work and appear professional, making them seem legitimate. The emails eventually request payment, typically around $250, for supposed production costs. Misericordia University history professor Jennifer Black initially felt excited about the invitation but grew suspicious when the email came directly from Gross herself rather than a producer, and when artificial intelligence seemed evident in the messaging.

WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have confirmed awareness of the fraudulent emails and are working with law enforcement to investigate. The scam has also targeted other celebrities including comedians Nikki Glaser and Amy Poehler and journalist Katie Couric. WHYY stated it never charges guests for interviews and that any communication requesting payment should be considered fraudulent. Cybersecurity experts advise people to verify requests through official contact information and to be skeptical of any requests for money or personal credentials, as artificial intelligence now enables convincingly personalized scams that target specific individuals based on their public profiles.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
A fake American think tank funded by Israel published over 560,000 words in nine days to influence artificial intelligence chatbots into promoting pro-Israel arguments. The Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not legally exist, created 124 reports framed as academic research addressing contentious topics like alleged Israeli war crimes and genocide in Gaza. The reports were strategically designed to appear in chatbot training data and search results, using a platform called Res that specializes in "generative engine optimization" to ensure AI systems cite the content.

The operation represents part of a broader Israeli government campaign costing tens of millions of dollars, routed through advertising company Havas Media and contractors including Trump's former campaign manager Brad Parscale. The Hanover Institute was registered with the US Justice Department as foreign agent propaganda material in August 2026. Israeli officials have expressed frustration about the campaign's ineffectiveness, with public opinion polling showing Americans increasingly sympathize with Palestinians rather than Israel. Researchers warn the effort demonstrates a new threat of foreign governments manipulating AI systems to shape online narratives without detection or fact-checking capability.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, and Warner Music have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno, alleging they scraped thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their models. The labels claim both companies deliberately concealed which music they used for training and argue that the companies' business model fundamentally relies on copyright infringement. The record labels submitted thousands of specific songs they say were copied, including works by The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Michael Jackson, and many others.

To support their claims, the record labels created AI-generated songs using highly specific prompts and compared the outputs to original copyrighted music. They documented numerous examples where the AI systems produced songs that directly replicated distinctive melodies, rhythms, and styles from famous recordings. One example involved generating a near-identical version of Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You," while another reproduced Green Day's "American Idiot" complete with original lyrics. The lawsuits were filed in New York against Udio and Massachusetts against Suno, setting up a major legal battle over how generative AI services should handle copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements to resolve disputes over copyright infringement. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs, including The Temptations' "My Girl," to train its artificial intelligence model without permission. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that uses only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create original songs from text prompts while ensuring artists and songwriters receive compensation.

This settlement marks Udio's first major licensing deal with a major record label and reflects the music industry's broader efforts to regulate AI technology. Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, had previously defended its technology as similar to how musicians learn from studying existing work. The company declined to disclose financial terms but stated that artists can opt into the new platform and will be compensated for their contributions.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
State Farm's defense lawyers apologized after admitting they used artificial intelligence to prepare legal filings that contained fabricated case citations, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings in a lawsuit brought by Los Angeles homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga. The homeowner sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable, and subsequent water damage and delays in repair approvals left her family bankrupt and homeless. Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson acknowledged that seven case citations across eight filings did not actually exist and used an AI tool called Irys, which she mistakenly believed would verify citations.

The discovery highlighted a growing problem in the legal field as 41% of law firms and 47% of corporate legal departments now use generative AI. A Paris-based database has documented nearly 1,900 cases of AI-generated legal hallucinations worldwide, mostly in the United States. State Farm said it expects external counsel to meet highest ethical standards and confirm accuracy, while the case is scheduled to proceed to trial in October.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: The 3 Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks for September
stories.Summary:
September typically presents challenging conditions for stock market investors, as the month historically experiences more declining periods than any other month for the S&P 500 and generally produces negative long-term returns. Despite these seasonal headwinds, the article identifies three artificial intelligence stocks positioned as attractive buying opportunities this month, suggesting investors should purchase them soon.

The three recommended stocks are Nvidia, Micron, and Amazon. Nvidia recently reported exceptional second quarter earnings with 106% year-over-year revenue growth and management guidance for 70% revenue growth in the following fiscal year. Micron manufactures memory chips experiencing high demand and supply shortages, with the company expecting market tightness to persist until 2028 while new production facilities come online. The stock trades at just six times fiscal 2027 earnings. Amazon is investing heavily in its cloud computing division AWS with 220 billion dollars in capital expenditures, and AWS growth accelerated from 28% to 37% year-over-year between quarters, now representing 60% of company operating income.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.

stories.Headline: 《TAIPEI TIMES》 Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040 - 焦點
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

During a meeting at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi, president of Saudi Arabia's Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority, discussed ways to establish a comprehensive and sustainable cooperation between the two nations.

Khawaja presented Pakistan's current initiatives to advance its national artificial intelligence and data governance agenda, while emphasizing the country's dedication to building a robust data ecosystem and strengthening its digital economy. The officials agreed to continue their discussions to further strengthen the partnership in these technology areas.

India is hosting its first dedicated summit focused on artificial intelligence in marketing in September 2026. The AIM Summit will take place on September 17 in Bengaluru and September 18 in New Delhi, bringing together over 50 chief marketing officers from major brands including Paytm, KFC, Nestle, and Uniqlo. The event expects to attract more than 600 marketing professionals as attendees and delegates.

The summit aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence and instead focus on practical implementation and real-world applications. The program will include an AI Lab for hands-on exploration of technology capabilities, an exhibition showcasing marketing solution providers, and an awards ceremony recognizing innovative organizations. Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics. The summit is being organized with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 executives across India.

stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.
